perf.summary: Con and H setters do a read-modify-write of packedData even when SetCon already maintains the invariant; H setter's '(value & 0xFF) << 24' on a uint is fine but the Con write path is exercised once per SetCon call.
perf.currentCost: SetCon (Recast.cs) already computes the full new 24-bit con value with its own masking, then assigns span->Con = ..., which re-enters the Con setter and does '(packedData & 0xFF000000) | (value & 0x00FFFFFF)' — a second load of packedData and a second mask, redundant with the masking SetCon just performed.
perf.proposedChange: Expose an internal raw accessor (e.g. internal uint Packed { get; set; }) on RcCompactSpan so SetCon can do a single read-modify-write on the raw word: 'span->Packed = (packed & ~(0x3fu<<shift) & ~0... )' keeping the H byte intact, instead of round-tripping through the Con property which re-masks. The Con property assignment currently reloads packedData and re-applies a 24-bit mask SetCon's value already satisfies.
perf.rationale: Collapses two read-modify-write sequences (SetCon's compute + the property setter's mask/merge) into one, removing a redundant load and two AND/OR ops per SetCon. SetCon runs once per (span,direction) during BuildCompactHeightfield neighbor linking.
perf.risk: Must preserve that the high byte (H, bits 24-31) is never clobbered. The single-RMW form must AND-clear only the 6 target bits within the low 24 and OR the new value, leaving bits 24-31 untouched — exactly what the current two-step does. Keep the public Con/H properties unchanged for API/interop; only add an internal raw path. Memory layout is unaffected (still one uint).
